deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematical derivation on this page. It is a bookkeeping record, continuing the list on the previous page, which carries the heading 'Ostgoth. 1850 1/11 VIII'. The heading '1852 1/5' is a date written as day/month: 1 May 1852. Previous entries are dated 1/11 (1 November) and 1/5 (1 May) of 1850 and 1851, so the entries are semi-annual. Each line has three parts: a count, a series letter (A, B, C, D), and an ascending list of serial numbers. These are almost certainly the numbers of bonds or loan certificates drawn for redemption in a periodic amortization lottery (Verlosung). Gauss kept such records for his securities investments. My reading of the record:
- 1 May 1852, series A: 6 numbers — 618, 673, 704, 811, 839, 908.
- Series B: 11 numbers — 285, 412, 442, 484, 671, 711, 1305, 1638, 1692, 1869, 1988.
- Series C: 14 numbers — 173, 328, 384, 512, 631, 658, 762, 863, 964, 1019, 1638, 1640, 1825, 1836.
- Series D: 14 numbers — 91, 168, 368, 1138, 1231, 1376, 1382, 1446, 1511, 1686, 1774, 1860, 1894, 1982.
In each series the leading count equals the number of serial numbers listed, so the leading figures are tallies (my inference). The total drawn is 6+11+14+14 = 45. The B and C numbers stay below 2000, and A here stays below 1000. This suggests series of about 1000 (A) and 2000 (B, C, D) pieces (my inference). The quotas per series change between drawings: earlier 5/12/12/13, then 5/12/13/13, then 6/11/13/13, now 6/11/14/14. That pattern fits an amortization plan in which drawings vary with the outstanding principal of each series.
errors: No errors were found. Each count matches its list (6, 11, 14, 14), and every list is strictly increasing. The number 1638 appears in both B and C, which is fine because they are separate series.
